title: Level 2 Exam
practical: The Level 2 practical assessment (run 3 missions and 2 fault recoveries) is completed in person with an instructor. This written exam is the first part.

questions.question: You have just powered on a unit and want to assign a mission. What should you confirm first?
options: That another unit has finished its own mission and the whole fleet is idle
That MoRo is in a ready state and its intended path is genuinely clear
That a supervisor has signed the mission off in writing
questions.feedback: Correct. Readiness and a clear path are the standard pre-checks before assigning any mission.

questions.question: A mission is running, but its status has stopped updating as you would expect. What does this call for?
options: Checking in, since a stall or non-updating status is a signal to look closer
Ignoring it, since missions always resolve on their own
Cancelling the mission immediately and powering the unit off
questions.feedback: Correct. Knowing what normal looks like is what lets you notice this kind of deviation.

questions.question: A colleague has just modified an existing mission. What should happen before it is treated as routine?
options: It can go straight into routine use because the change was small
It should be run once under direct supervision first
It should be validated only after it has failed once in service
questions.feedback: Correct. Any new or modified mission should be validated under supervision first.

questions.question: Which of these best describes the structure of a mission?
options: A continuous process that runs all shift with no completion condition
A set of joystick commands recorded by an operator
A defined start, a defined objective, and a defined end state
questions.feedback: Correct. Every mission has a clear start, objective, and end state.

questions.question: A mission fails to complete. What is the operator's standard first response?
options: Run a full technical diagnosis before telling anyone else about the failure
Note what happened, assess whether it is safe, and escalate if unclear
Reassign the mission repeatedly until it succeeds, without checking anything
questions.feedback: Correct. Diagnosis is not required at the operator level; note, assess, and escalate.

questions.question: Which of these is a payload configuration MoRo supports?
options: Hydraulic crane arm
Pneumatic sorting chute
Lift-and-rotate
questions.feedback: Correct. Supported configurations are conveyor, cobot interface, towing, lifting, and lift-and-rotate.

questions.question: Two systems exchange signals confirming readiness, completion, and any error state before either one acts. What is this called?
options: A map update
A mission validation
A handshake
questions.feedback: Correct. A handshake makes sure neither system acts before the other is genuinely ready.

questions.question: During a handoff at a CNC station, MoRo appears to have stopped. What should an operator present confirm before walking away?
options: That MoRo's battery has charged to full before it leaves the station
That the payload attachment has been removed
That both systems show a ready or completing state
questions.feedback: Correct. Confirm the exchange actually succeeded rather than assuming it did.

questions.question: Why does a loaded MoRo need extra clearance compared with an empty one?
options: A loaded unit always travels faster than an empty one, which needs more room to react
The load shifts its center of gravity, which affects stopping behavior and stability
The load switches off its interactive zone
questions.feedback: Correct. Weight distribution changes how the unit stops and how stable it is.

questions.question: A payload attachment looks misaligned. What should you do?
options: Press it firmly into position and continue the mission
Cancel the mission and re-run it without the attachment
Not force it into place; note the issue and escalate
questions.feedback: Correct. Forcing a misaligned attachment risks damage; escalation is the right response.

questions.question: Which battery chemistry do all MoRo variants use?
options: LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate)
Lead-acid, as used in older industrial trucks
Nickel-cadmium
questions.feedback: Correct. LFP is confirmed across the A-250, A-500, and A-1200.

questions.question: What runtime and charging figures are confirmed across all MoRo variants?
options: 4 hours of runtime, with cable charging overnight
12 hours of runtime, with charging in about 20 minutes from a standard dock
8 hours of runtime, with wireless charging in under 1 hour
questions.feedback: Correct. Runtime is 8 hours and wireless charging takes under 1 hour.

questions.question: A unit is sitting on its dock, but its status indicator does not show it charging. What is the right response?
options: Assume it is charging and leave it until the end of the shift
Flag it instead of assuming charging is underway
Replace the battery yourself before the next mission
questions.feedback: Correct. A docked unit that is not visibly charging is worth flagging.

questions.question: Which charging habit supports longer battery life?
options: Letting every unit run completely flat before it is sent back to charge
Charging only once a day, overnight, so the pack is always full at the start
Opportunistic charging windows during the shift, not full depletion
questions.feedback: Correct. Consistent, moderate charging supports longer battery health.

questions.question: At the operator level, what is your role in battery health?
options: Awareness and reporting; detailed diagnosis belongs to L3A technicians
Performing cell-level diagnostics yourself whenever a battery seems to be weak
Replacing batteries whenever they seem weak
questions.feedback: Correct. Detailed battery diagnostics belong to the technician-level curriculum.

questions.question: A fleet system distributes missions among several units. Which factors does it use?
options: The color of each unit and the time of day
Proximity, availability, and current load
The order in which the units were purchased
questions.feedback: Correct. Task assignment is largely automatic, based on proximity, availability, and load.

questions.question: Who manages collision avoidance between several MoRo units sharing a floor?
options: The fleet management system, automatically
The operator, unit by unit
Each unit independently, with no awareness of the others
questions.feedback: Correct. Units are aware of each other's positions and the fleet system coordinates their paths.

questions.question: Which description matches a deadlock?
options: Two or more units each waiting for the other to move, with neither able to proceed
A unit stopping because its battery is low, so it has left the queue to head for the dock
A mission paused deliberately by an operator
questions.feedback: Correct. A deadlock is a mutual wait between units.

questions.question: What is the difference between a shared path and a reserved route?
options: A shared path is for people to walk on and a reserved route is for MoRo units only
A shared path is used only for charging and a reserved route is used only for maintenance
Shared paths serve many units; reserved routes prioritize specific traffic
questions.feedback: Correct. Zone structure keeps throughput efficient as the fleet grows.

questions.question: Two units appear mutually stalled for longer than expected. What should you do?
options: Wait indefinitely, because deadlocks between units always clear by themselves
Flag it rather than assuming it will always resolve itself
Push one unit out of the way by hand
questions.feedback: Correct. The fleet system usually resolves deadlocks, but a prolonged stall is worth flagging.

questions.question: MoRo keeps stopping in an area that should be clear. What is a reasonable first check?
options: Clean and recalibrate the LiDAR yourself straight away to restore its full accuracy
Look for something physically blocking a sensor, without adjusting it yourself
Disable the interactive zone for that area until the cause is found
questions.feedback: Correct. Check for obvious causes, but leave sensor work to those trained and authorized.

questions.question: A unit stops accepting new missions and is unresponsive on the dashboard. What might this indicate?
options: That its battery chemistry has failed
A connectivity problem rather than necessarily a hardware fault
That its map has been deleted
questions.feedback: Correct. Dashboard unresponsiveness often points to connectivity.

questions.question: Which details are useful to gather before escalating an issue?
options: What MoRo was doing, what its status shows, and any change in the environment
Only the unit's serial number and the date it was last serviced
Only the time the shift started and the name of the operator who was on duty at the time
questions.feedback: Correct. This context speeds up the technician's eventual diagnosis.

questions.question: A mission has failed. Which detail best narrows the likely cause for whoever picks up the diagnosis?
options: Which operator assigned the mission and at what time of the shift it was assigned
How many missions ran earlier that day and how long each of them took
Where in the mission it failed (start, mid-route, destination)
questions.feedback: Correct. Where in the mission it failed significantly narrows the likely causes.

questions.question: A brief pause clears by itself and a single retry succeeds. What is the right call?
options: No escalation is needed
Escalate immediately as a critical fault
Shut the unit down for the rest of the shift
questions.feedback: Correct. Issues that resolve within a normal operational pattern do not need escalation.

questions.question: Which description matches conditional logic in a mission?
options: The mission runs the same steps regardless of conditions
The next action depends on whether a specified condition is met
The mission repeats forever with no end state
questions.feedback: Correct. Conditional logic lets a mission branch based on conditions.

questions.question: What does cycle time measure?
options: How long a mission takes from start to finish
How much material is moved over the course of a month
How long a battery takes to charge
questions.feedback: Correct. Cycle time is mission duration; throughput is how much gets moved over a period.

questions.question: A mission still completes but now takes noticeably longer than usual. What should you do at L2?
options: Ignore it, because it still completes
Rewrite the route yourself
Mention it, since it can signal something worth investigating
questions.feedback: Correct. A slowdown is useful information even when the mission succeeds.

questions.question: A route looks inefficient to you. What is the right awareness at L2?
options: It may reflect constraints, such as safety zones or other unit traffic, that you cannot see
It is almost certainly a mistake and should be changed right away by the operator on shift
Routes are chosen at random
questions.feedback: Correct. Routes and speeds are chosen deliberately; detailed optimization belongs to L3B.

questions.question: Does MoRo's data logging need operator action?
options: No, it logs mission timing and completion status automatically
Yes, the operator must record every mission by hand after it completes
Only when a mission fails
questions.feedback: Correct. Logging happens automatically during operation.
